newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: France lends Burkina Faso $11 mln for rail refit.
newsitem.headline: France lends Burkina Faso $11 mln for rail refit.

text.p: France has lent the state company that owns Burkina Faso's rail network 5.7 billion CFA francs to boost investment in the dilapidated line that links the landlocked West African nation to the sea via Ivory Coast.

The Caisse Francaise de Developpement granted the loan on Friday to SOPAFER-B within the framework of the privatisation of the running of the loss-making line which was taken over in August 1995 by specially formed private company SITARAIL.

French transit and transport group SAGA heads a consortium of private companies holding a stake of 65 percent in SITARAIL, which was granted a concession to run the line by Burkina Faso and Ivory Coast in 1994.

The loan will help pay for renovating track, buildings, equipment, communications and other infrastructure on the line from Ivory Coast's main port and commercial capital Abidjan via Burkina Faso's capital Ouagadougou to Kaya.
